text.tspan: A functor 𝐹: 𝓝₁ → 𝓝₂ sends each object n ∈ 𝓝₁ to an object 𝐹(n) ∈ 𝓝₂. It must send morphisms
in 𝓝₁ to morphisms in 𝓝₂. This means if there is a morphism m → n then there had better be a
morphism 𝐹(m) → 𝐹(n). A picture to have in mind is:
Notice there are no equations in either of the preceding categories. The monotone map (functor) is
the blue arrows. Finally, notice that 𝓝₁ and 𝓝₂ have both the same objects and the morphisms, so
𝓝₁ = 𝓝₂ = 𝓝 (an endomorphism). Thinking in Cat we have:
